title: Movie Storyboard Animator
style: Realistic cinematic explainer, natural lighting, subtle film grain, shallow depth of field, modern indie studio environment, clean practical effects, energetic but grounded mood, consistent color palette of warm amber desk lights and cool blue monitor glow.

character.description: A focused indie movie director in his early 30s, medium build, tousled dark hair, light stubble, round glasses, black t-shirt under an olive overshirt, wearing a lanyard with blank badge. He works in a cluttered but creative home studio with storyboards, camera gear, sticky notes, a laptop, and editing monitors.
continuityRules: The director must keep the same face, hair, glasses, clothing, and lanyard in every shot.
Use the same studio location with recurring motifs: corkboard storyboard panels, scattered sticky notes, film clapboard, laptop, timeline monitor, and warm desk lamp.
No real brand logos, exact software interfaces, or copyrighted marks; use generic screens and fictional UI.
Clones are identical versions of the director with slight pose differences but the same outfit and appearance.

references.prompt: Realistic character reference portrait of an indie movie director in his early 30s, medium build, tousled dark hair, light stubble, round glasses, black t-shirt under olive overshirt, blank lanyard badge, focused expression, cinematic studio lighting, neutral background, high detail, no logos.

Realistic modern indie filmmaker home studio, corkboard filled with storyboard sketches, sticky notes, camera gear, laptop, dual editing monitors with generic timelines, film clapboard, warm desk lamp, cool blue monitor glow, cinematic clutter, no visible brand logos.

shots.title: The Manual Grind
shots.caption: Making longer AI videos is still painful.
shots.narration: Most video models stop at short clips, and assembling everything by hand becomes tedious.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic wide shot of the indie director alone in his cluttered home studio at night, hunched over a desk with dual monitors showing generic fragmented video clips and a messy timeline, coffee mug, sticky notes, and a film clapboard nearby. His face shows frustration, warm desk lamp on one side, cool monitor glow on the other, no logos.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic close shot from over the director's shoulder, his hands dragging many tiny generic clip blocks across a chaotic editing timeline on a monitor, shoulders tense, storyboard papers scattered around the keyboard, the studio still lit by amber lamp and blue screen glow, no logos.
shots.videoPrompt: Slow push-in from wide studio view to over-the-shoulder monitor view. The director sighs, rubs his forehead, then drags short clip blocks across the generic timeline. Papers shift slightly, monitor glow flickers, maintain realistic motion and continuity.

shots.title: Fifteen-Second Ceiling
shots.caption: Short clips. Long assembly.
shots.narration: Each idea turns into a pile of disconnected fragments.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic medium shot of the director standing before a wall of floating printed frame thumbnails and sticky notes, each labeled only with generic numbers like shot 01, shot 02, shot 03. He looks overwhelmed, holding a marker, with the corkboard storyboard behind him and studio lights glowing softly.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic close shot of the director's hand holding a marker near a storyboard card that reads 15 sec max in handwritten text, surrounded by many small clip thumbnails connected with red string, his blurred concerned face in the background, no logos.
shots.videoPrompt: Camera slides laterally across the wall of storyboard cards and clip thumbnails. The director steps into frame, scans the clutter, then circles the handwritten 15 sec max note. Keep motion subtle, documentary-style, realistic.

shots.title: The Storyboard Spark
shots.caption: Break the movie into shots first.
shots.narration: Then he sees the answer hiding in the storyboard itself.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic medium shot of the director seated at the desk, exhausted, looking from the chaotic monitor toward a neat physical storyboard pinned on the corkboard. The studio is quiet, warm lamp light catching the storyboard panels, blue monitor glow behind him.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic close-up of the director smiling with sudden inspiration, eyes reflected in his round glasses. Behind him, the storyboard panels appear orderly and clear, with simple sketch boxes, arrows, and duration notes, no logos or real software.
shots.videoPrompt: Gentle rack focus from the messy monitor to the neat storyboard. The director slowly turns his head, expression shifts from frustration to realization. Camera pushes toward his inspired face, with a soft light bloom from the desk lamp.

shots.title: Script Becomes Structure
shots.caption: A script becomes a shot plan.
shots.narration: The concept can be structured once into shots, keyframes, motion, and timing.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic over-the-desk shot of the director typing a movie concept into a clean fictional interface on a laptop. Around the laptop are storyboard cards, a pencil, and a clapboard. The screen shows generic blocks labeled title, style, characters, shots, start frame, end frame, motion.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic close shot of the laptop screen displaying a clean fictional JSON-like storyboard layout with organized shot cards, durations, keyframe prompts, and motion prompts, reflected faintly in the director's glasses at the edge of frame, no logos.
shots.videoPrompt: Camera tilts down from the director typing to the laptop screen. Text blocks animate into neat shot cards, transforming from messy notes into structured fields. Keep UI fictional, clean, and readable without real brand references.

shots.title: Many Shots, One Vision
shots.caption: Split the work while keeping continuity.
shots.narration: Each shot can be generated separately, while references keep the look consistent.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic wide shot of the director standing in the center of the studio, holding a stack of storyboard cards. Around him, faint ghosted duplicates of himself begin to appear, each identical in clothing and appearance, the corkboard and monitors behind them glowing.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic wide shot of five identical director clones working at different stations in the same studio: one sketching storyboard cards, one reviewing character reference images, one arranging keyframes, one checking motion notes, one organizing clips. All clones look like the same director, no logos.
shots.videoPrompt: Use a smooth orbiting camera move as the director fans out storyboard cards. Ghosted duplicates materialize into solid clones and move to separate workstations. Maintain consistent actor appearance, realistic lighting, and seamless practical-effects feel.

shots.title: Keyframes Come Alive
shots.caption: Start frame. End frame. Motion between.
shots.narration: Every shot gets a start image, an end image, and a clear motion direction.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic medium shot of one director clone holding two printed keyframe images labeled start and end in simple handwritten text. The images show a generic cinematic scene evolving from one composition to another. Other clones work in the softly blurred studio background.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic close shot of the two printed keyframes placed into a glowing tabletop workflow board, with a smooth arrow drawn between them labeled motion. The director clone's hands align the cards carefully, warm lamp light and blue monitor glow reflecting on the table.
shots.videoPrompt: Camera pushes in as the clone places the start and end keyframes onto the tabletop board. A subtle animated arrow glows between them, suggesting motion interpolation. Hands move carefully, papers slide naturally, continuity remains realistic.

shots.title: The Clips Return
shots.caption: Completed clips arrive in order.
shots.narration: The separated tasks come back as finished animated shots.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic shot of the main director at the central desk, looking up as identical clones approach from different parts of the studio carrying small glowing film reels, tablets, and clip cards. The atmosphere is productive and organized.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic close wide shot of the desk filled with neatly arranged clip cards labeled shot 01 through shot 06, each with a tiny generic thumbnail image. The clones stand around the desk, satisfied, while the main director reviews the ordered sequence.
shots.videoPrompt: Camera tracks backward as clones converge toward the desk and place completed clip cards in order. The main director nods, arranges them into a clean sequence, and the chaotic workspace now feels organized.

shots.title: The Assembly Machine
shots.caption: Assemble once. Export one movie.
shots.narration: The pipeline assembles the shots in order into one continuous movie.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic shot of the director feeding ordered clip cards into a whimsical but believable desktop assembly machine made of metal trays, rollers, lights, and a small screen showing a generic progress bar. The machine sits beside the laptop in the same studio, no logos.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic shot of a single glowing film strip emerging from the assembly machine, showing connected scenes as one continuous movie. The director watches with relief and pride, clones fading into the background, warm and cool studio lights balanced.
shots.videoPrompt: Camera follows the clip cards as they slide into the machine. Rollers turn, indicator lights pulse, and a continuous film strip emerges. The director leans in, smiling slightly, while the clones become less prominent behind him.

shots.title: One Continuous Film
shots.caption: From idea to finished video.
shots.narration: A longer story becomes manageable, shot by shot.
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic wide shot of the director dimming the studio lights and facing a large monitor. The completed film plays as a generic cinematic montage on screen, reflected in his glasses. Storyboard cards and clip cards are now neatly stacked on the desk.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Realistic rear shot of the director centered before the large monitor, watching a smooth continuous movie timeline with connected shots. The studio feels calm and complete, warm desk lamp still glowing, no logos or real interface details.
shots.videoPrompt: Slow dolly behind the director as he sits back and watches the finished movie. The monitor displays a seamless generic montage, with soft screen flicker on his silhouette. The scene settles into calm completion.

shots.title: Final Slogan
shots.caption: Easy script to movie conversion
shots.startKeyframePrompt: Realistic cinematic shot of the director standing beside the corkboard, now clean and organized with storyboard cards flowing into a single film strip graphic. The studio lighting is polished, with warm amber highlights and cool blue accents, no logos.
shots.endKeyframePrompt: Clean realistic hero shot of the studio desk and monitor with large readable on-screen text: Easy script to movie conversion. The director stands slightly off to the side, confident and calm, storyboard cards and film strip motif visible, cinematic lighting, no logos.
shots.videoPrompt: Camera slowly pushes toward the final monitor as the storyboard cards visually align into one film strip. The slogan fades in clearly and holds. The director remains still and confident, with realistic lighting and a polished explainer ending.
